title: The July 2020 NAVO warm offset remains within fixed geographic and day-night groups
abstract: We tested whether changed geographic sampling explains the July 2020 NAVO MetOp-A warm offset against ESA SST CCI at 60 S to 60 N. We used published daily bins and matched 29 earlier and 25 later dates between 2019 and 2020. An exact decomposition on fixed 5-degree day-night strata gives a within-stratum change of +0.069 C. A conditional 95% block-weight interval is +0.051 to +0.089 C. Redistribution between strata contributes -0.010 C (-0.025 to +0.003 C). These terms sum to a pixel-weighted change of +0.059 C. Fixed area weights give +0.081 C. The within-stratum offset persists at night, with quality level 5 only, and on 1- and 10-degree grids. The main support retains more than 98% of pixels. Broad geographic redistribution cannot explain the offset under this comparison. Selection within cells and retrieval changes remain unresolved. One control year, missing dates, inherited satellite bins and reference errors limit causal inference. Code, source hashes, aggregate results, time-weight draws and numerical audits are included.

display.caption: The July 2020 warm change remains within fixed 5-degree geographic and illumination groups. Bars show conditional 95% block-weight intervals. Redistribution has an uncertain sign.

citations.reason: Uses verified daily NAVO-minus-CCI count and sum bins to test the unresolved geographic sampling mechanism.
